titel: Ageing meat: why aged meat is more tender
kurz: After slaughter, the meat's own [[enzym|enzymes]] slowly break down the fibres. The meat becomes more tender and, when dry-aged, more savoury too.
bild_im_kopf: Like a new pair of leather shoes that softens over time: stiff at first, comfortable after weeks.
was_passiert: Right after slaughter, muscle meat is stiff. Over the following days and weeks, enzymes in the meat itself loosen the fibres. When dry-ageing on the bone, water also evaporates, the flavour concentrates and nutty, cheesy aromas develop. The outer, dried-out layer is trimmed off.
warum_wichtig: Explains why aged beef is more expensive and more tender, and why fresh meat from the farm sometimes turns out tough.
faustregeln: For quick-cooked beef, choose aged meat.
Dry-age at home only with a dedicated fridge and large pieces, not steaks.
Meat aged in a vacuum bag becomes more tender, but not more savoury.

stellschrauben.wirkung: longer → more tender, more savoury, more loss

praxis.text: A rib-eye aged for three to four weeks is noticeably more tender than a fresh one.
